definition-changed.answer: The rule uses 'procedure division' (the division), never the defined term 'procedure'; §2002:4 (entry 4.150) 'One or more successive paragraphs or sections in the procedure division' vs §2023:3.145 does not touch what the division is. Scope and evidence unchanged.

definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 (entry 4.163) defines report as the printed output described in the report section; 2023 drops the entry and the term rests on the RD entry and REPORT clause (§2023:13.18.46.1). In both editions a report is exactly what one RD describes, so the rule governs the same report groups and RDs. 'report description entry' is the RD in both.

pending-clause.answer: §2002:8.4.1.1 differs from 2023 in its formats 1-3 (file-cd-report-qualifier with cd-name-1) and in one general sentence: 'The LINAGE-COUNTER and report counter identifiers require qualification ... whenever a SOURCE UNIT would result in more than one occurrence', where SR8 says source ELEMENT (§2002:4 (entry 4.172)). SR8 does not rest on that sentence: its own words fix its scope (more than one RD in the source element), identical to the 2023 rule, and format 8 is identical. The sentence's wider reading (a contained program's RD) is resolved in 2002 by scope of names: counters are local unless the RD is GLOBAL (§2002:8.4.5.1.4) and an inner declaration wins (§2002:8.4.5.1 (item 3a)). Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/op-20261114/read-2002/out-answer/probes-a-11/lc-nested.cob (outer GLOBAL RD R1 + inner RD R2, unqualified LINE-COUNTER in each; PAGE-COUNTER follows the same scope rule 8.4.5.1.4): accepted and the same at --std 2002 and 2023 (lc-nested.log). The sentence is the pending clause's own question, not this row's.
